To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose two models for QoS-based service selection: combinatorial model (MMKP) and graph model (MCOP); we design efficient algorithms for service selection with end-to- end QoS constraints; and we compare the two models and analyze the pros and cons of each.
we propose efficient algorithms for Web services composition with QoS constraints.
we have developed efficient algorithms for service composition with QoS constraints.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to select services to maximize the application-specific utility under the end-to end QoS constraints.

how to select services with QoS guarantees in the presence of multiple QoS attributes, how to select services to meet the QoS constraints, and how to select services for different types of service composition structures.
efficient algorithms for service selection in SOA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for a given problem, the graph model is more efficient than the combinatorial one, but the latter is more suitable when there are many constraints.
, in terms of the efficiency of the solution, the combinatorial approach is more effective for the case of a single service composition structure.

the combinatorial approach is more suitable for the selection of service processes with small number of service components, while the graph approach is more suitable when the number of service components is large.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combinatorial approach is better than the graph approach when the number of service candidates is small.
the combinatorial models are more flexible in modeling the QoS-based service selection problem and the graph models are more efficient for the service processes of simple structures.
we propose a broker-based architecture and efficient algorithms for service selection with end-toend QoS constraints.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the graph model is better than the combinatorial one when the service composition is a directed acyclic graph.
the graph model is a better choice than the combinatorial one for the service selection problem, since it can be used to model more complex service composition structures and is easier to implement.
the MCOP model is a good approximation for the MMKP model.
